/-!
# Conjecture 10.38

by G. A. Noskov

(W. van der Kallen). Does $E_{n+3}(\mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n])$, $n \geq 1$, have finite
breadth with respect to the set of transvections?

Here $E_m(R)$ is the elementary subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_m(R)$: the subgroup generated by the
(elementary) transvections $1 + c\,e_{ij}$, where $i \neq j$, $c \in R$ and $e_{ij}$ is the
matrix unit with a single $1$ in position $(i, j)$. A group has finite breadth (also called
finite width) with respect to a set of generators $S$ if there is a uniform bound $N$ such that
every element of the group is a product of at most $N$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$. The set of
transvections is closed under inversion, so here this means a product of at most $N$
transvections.

The question is motivated by van der Kallen's theorem that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{C}[x])$ does
not have bounded word length with respect to the elementary transvections.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- W. van der Kallen, *$SL_3(\mathbb{C}[X])$ does not have bounded word length*,
  Algebraic K-theory, Part I (Oberwolfach, 1980), Lecture Notes in Math. 966,
  Springer, 1982, 357–361.
-/

justification.closest_existing_considered: Matrix.transvection / Matrix.TransvectionStruct (Mathlib) — these give the matrices but only in the monoid Matrix m m R, not as a subset of a group; no Mathlib set/subgroup of transvections exists.

justification.why_needed: The set of elementary transvections 1 + c·e_{ij} (i ≠ j, c ∈ R) as elements of SL_m(R) is needed both as the generating set of E_m(R) and as the set with respect to which breadth is measured. transvections $1 + c\,e_{ij}$, $i \neq j$. -/

def HasFiniteBreadth {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) (S : Set G) : Prop :=
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ g ∈ H, ∃ L : List G, (∀ s ∈ L, s ∈ S) ∧ L.length ≤ N ∧ L.prod = g
blocks.docstring:
A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ has finite breadth (width) with respect to a set $S \subseteq G$
if there is a uniform bound $N$ such that every element of $H$ is a product of at most $N$
elements of $S$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib for width / word length / bounded generation; nothing found. Subgroup.closure alone does not express a uniform length bound.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.38».HasFiniteBreadth
justification.why_needed: 'Finite breadth (width) with respect to a set S' — ∃ N, every element of the subgroup H is a product of at most N elements of S (as a List G with all entries in S, length ≤ N, and prod = g). No width/word-length-boundedness notion exists in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: HasFiniteBreadth
blocks.text:
/-- A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ has finite breadth (width) with respect to a set $S \subseteq G$
if there is a uniform bound $N$ such that every element of $H$ is a product of at most $N$
elements of $S$. -/
def HasFiniteBreadth {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) (S : Set G) : Prop :=
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ g ∈ H, ∃ L : List G, (∀ s ∈ L, s ∈ S) ∧ L.length ≤ N ∧ L.prod = g

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma one_mem_elementaryTransvections [Nontrivial m] :
    (1 : SpecialLinearGroup m R) ∈ elementaryTransvections m R := by
  obtain ⟨i, j, hij⟩ := exists_pair_ne m
  exact ⟨i, j, 0, hij, by simp⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma inv_mem_elementaryTransvections {g : SpecialLinearGroup m R}
    (hg : g ∈ elementaryTransvections m R) : g⁻¹ ∈ elementaryTransvections m R := by
  obtain ⟨i, j, c, hij, hg⟩ := hg
  refine ⟨i, j, -c, hij, ?_⟩
  have h : g * ⟨transvection i j (-c), det_transvection_of_ne i j hij (-c)⟩ = 1 := by
    ext1
    simp [hg, transvection_mul_transvection_same i j hij]
  rw [inv_eq_of_mul_eq_one_right h]

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question: 'finite breadth (width) with respect to transvections' means there is a uniform bound N such that every element of the elementary subgroup E_{n+3}(Z[x_1,...,x_n]) (the group generated by the elementary transvections 1 + c·e_{ij}, i ≠ j, c ∈ Z[x_1,...,x_n]) is a product of at most N such transvections; the condition 'n ≥ 1' is an implicit universal quantifier over the polynomial-ring parameter n (matrix size n+3 is tied to the number n of variables), so the Prop is answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 1, ∃ N, every element of E_{n+3}(ℤ[x_1,…,x_n]) is a product of ≤ N transvections (Mathlib's Matrix.transvection can serve as the generator set; note the bound N may depend on n).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates encode the same faithful content: ring ℤ[x₁,…,xₙ] = MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ, matrix size Fin (n+3), generators = elementary transvections 1 + c·e_{ij} with i ≠ j (Mathlib's Matrix.transvection / TransvectionStruct), E_{n+3} = Subgroup.closure (or equivalently, in c01/c02, the set of finite transvection products), breadth = ∃ N with every element a product of ≤ N transvections, quantified as answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 1, ∃ N (bound may depend on n). All compile warning-free. c04 chosen for readability and reviewability: named bespoke definitions (elementaryTransvections, elementarySubgroup, HasFiniteBreadth) with proven API lemmas, including inverse-closure of the transvection set (justifying products from S alone rather than S ∪ S⁻¹) and 1 ∈ S (so 'at most N' = 'exactly N'). My edits: module docstring now states the S ∪ S⁻¹ definition of width and why it coincides here, and adds the van der Kallen reference (SL₃(ℂ[x]) has unbounded word length) for context.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.38

by G. A. Noskov

(W. van der Kallen). Does $E_{n+3}(\mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n])$, $n \geq 1$, have finite
breadth with respect to the set of transvections?

Here $E_m(R)$ is the elementary subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_m(R)$: the subgroup generated by the
(elementary) transvections $1 + c\,e_{ij}$, where $i \neq j$, $c \in R$ and $e_{ij}$ is the
matrix unit with a single $1$ in position $(i, j)$. A group has finite breadth (also called
finite width) with respect to a set of generators $S$ if there is a uniform bound $N$ such that
every element of the group is a product of at most $N$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$. The set of
transvections is closed under inversion, so here this means a product of at most $N$
transvections.

The question is motivated by van der Kallen's theorem that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{C}[x])$ does
not have bounded word length with respect to the elementary transvections.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- W. van der Kallen, *$SL_3(\mathbb{C}[X])$ does not have bounded word length*,
  Algebraic K-theory, Part I (Oberwolfach, 1980), Lecture Notes in Math. 966,
  Springer, 1982, 357–361.
-/

open Matrix

namespace Kourovka.«10.38»

/-- The set of (elementary) transvections $1 + c\,e_{ij}$, with $i \neq j$ and $c \in R$, viewed
as elements of $\mathrm{SL}_m(R)$. -/
def elementaryTransvections (m R : Type*) [DecidableEq m] [Fintype m] [CommRing R] :
    Set (SpecialLinearGroup m R) :=
  {g | ∃ (i j : m) (c : R), i ≠ j ∧ (g : Matrix m m R) = transvection i j c}

/-- The elementary subgroup $E_m(R)$: the subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_m(R)$ generated by the
transvections $1 + c\,e_{ij}$, $i \neq j$. -/
def elementarySubgroup (m R : Type*) [DecidableEq m] [Fintype m] [CommRing R] :
    Subgroup (SpecialLinearGroup m R) :=
  Subgroup.closure (elementaryTransvections m R)

/-- A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ has finite breadth (width) with respect to a set $S \subseteq G$
if there is a uniform bound $N$ such that every element of $H$ is a product of at most $N$
elements of $S$. -/
def HasFiniteBreadth {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) (S : Set G) : Prop :=
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ g ∈ H, ∃ L : List G, (∀ s ∈ L, s ∈ S) ∧ L.length ≤ N ∧ L.prod = g

section API

variable {m R : Type*} [DecidableEq m] [Fintype m] [CommRing R]

/-- The identity matrix is a transvection (with $c = 0$) as soon as there are two distinct
indices. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma one_mem_elementaryTransvections [Nontrivial m] :
    (1 : SpecialLinearGroup m R) ∈ elementaryTransvections m R := by
  obtain ⟨i, j, hij⟩ := exists_pair_ne m
  exact ⟨i, j, 0, hij, by simp⟩

/-- The set of transvections is closed under inverses: $(1 + c\,e_{ij})^{-1} = 1 - c\,e_{ij}$.
Hence breadth with respect to this set does not depend on whether inverses of generators are
allowed. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma inv_mem_elementaryTransvections {g : SpecialLinearGroup m R}
    (hg : g ∈ elementaryTransvections m R) : g⁻¹ ∈ elementaryTransvections m R := by
  obtain ⟨i, j, c, hij, hg⟩ := hg
  refine ⟨i, j, -c, hij, ?_⟩
  have h : g * ⟨transvection i j (-c), det_transvection_of_ne i j hij (-c)⟩ = 1 := by
    ext1
    simp [hg, transvection_mul_transvection_same i j hij]
  rw [inv_eq_of_mul_eq_one_right h]

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma elementaryTransvections_subset_elementarySubgroup :
    elementaryTransvections m R ⊆ elementarySubgroup m R :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure

/-- The trivial subgroup has finite breadth with respect to any set. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
lemma hasFiniteBreadth_bot {G : Type*} [Group G] (S : Set G) :
    HasFiniteBreadth (⊥ : Subgroup G) S :=
  ⟨0, fun g hg => ⟨[], by simp, le_rfl, by simpa using hg.symm⟩⟩

end API

/--
(W. van der Kallen). Does $E_{n+3}(\mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n])$, $n \geq 1$, have finite
breadth with respect to the set of transvections?

That is, for every $n \geq 1$, is there a bound $N$ (which may depend on $n$) such that every
element of the elementary subgroup $E_{n+3}(\mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n])$ is a product of at
most $N$ transvections $1 + c\,e_{ij}$ with $i \neq j$ and $c \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 19 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.38» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
      HasFiniteBreadth (elementarySubgroup (Fin (n + 3)) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ))
        (elementaryTransvections (Fin (n + 3)) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.38»

items: 'Transvections' is interpreted as the elementary transvections 1 + c·e_{ij} (i ≠ j, c ∈ R), following van der Kallen's bounded-word-length setting and the decomposition table, not the more general 'transvections' 1 + u·vᵀ with vᵀu = 0.
E_{n+3}(R) is placed inside Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin (n+3)) R (as Subgroup.closure of the transvections); this is standard since every elementary transvection has determinant 1.

Breadth is measured by products of elements of the set S itself (no explicit inverses). This is equivalent to the usual word length over S ∪ S⁻¹ because the set of elementary transvections is closed under inverses ((1 + c e_{ij})⁻¹ = 1 − c e_{ij}); this is recorded by the API lemma inv_mem_elementaryTransvections. Since 1 ∈ S (c = 0), 'at most N' and 'exactly N' also coincide.
'n ≥ 1' is read as a universal quantifier: answer(True) iff for every n ≥ 1 the group E_{n+3}(ℤ[x_1,…,x_n]) has finite breadth; the bound N is allowed to depend on n (∃ N sits inside ∀ n).
ℤ[x_1,…,x_n] is formalized as MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ; the matrix index type is Fin (n+3), tying matrix size to the number of variables exactly as in the statement.
AMS tags 19 (K-theory: elementary subgroups / stability) and 20 (group theory) were chosen.

reviewer_notes: Interpretive choices (all fixed by the decomposition table and shared by every candidate): (1) 'transvections' = elementary transvections t_{ij}(c) = 1 + c e_{ij}, i ≠ j, not the broader class of GL-conjugates / unimodular transvections 1 + u·φ; (2) 'n ≥ 1' is read as a universal quantifier inside answer(sorry) ↔ …, so answer(True) means every E_{n+3}(ℤ[x₁,…,xₙ]) has finite breadth and answer(False) means some n ≥ 1 fails — a possible 'yes for some n, no for others' situation is collapsed to False, which is inherent to a single yes/no slot; (3) E_{n+3} is taken inside SL_{n+3} (all generators have det 1, so this is the same group). Boundary: n ≥ 1 is imposed as in the source (n = 0, E_3(ℤ), is excluded). No candidate omitted the slot; no objections to the decomposition were raised. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
